title: Reconstitution of melanocyte stem cells where the follicular reservoir is gone

concept.text: The proposed innovation is to rebuild a lasting, self-renewing supply of pigment-producing cells in human skin with documented loss of its follicular melanocyte reservoir, without donor tissue grafting. It would establish both differentiated melanocytes, which produce pigment, and a renewable precursor population that can replace them over time. Successful restoration would survive after any temporary immune treatment used during establishment ends.

The biological premise is that restoring pigmentation requires an adequate supply of melanocytes or their precursors together with a suitable immune environment. Hair follicles provide an important reservoir, but they are not the only possible source. White hair, hairless skin and longstanding disease can identify difficult treatment settings without proving that every usable precursor has disappeared. The target therefore requires documented follicular reservoir loss and evidence distinguishing newly established renewal from recruitment of surviving cells.

significance.text: If achieved, this capability would address a central limitation of reservoir-poor vitiligo: suppressing inflammation or stimulating pigmentation cannot reliably restore color when too few usable pigment cells remain. Its direct consequence would be repigmentation in the reservoir-depleted settings actually demonstrated, potentially including selected lesions with white hairs or glabrous acral skin. The advance would extend treatment beyond dependence on surviving local cells and donor grafts, while demonstrating that the restored pigment-cell population can renew itself.

Cell restoration and durable immune control address complementary obstacles. The supplied review supports combining melanocyte regeneration with an appropriate immune environment, and the 2025 primer abstract identifies tissue-resident memory T cells as central to vitiligo pathogenesis. Rebuilding cells that remain vulnerable to renewed immune attack could yield only temporary benefit; controlling attack where cells are depleted could leave insufficient material for repigmentation. Together these capabilities provide a rationale for lasting restoration, but neither their combination nor two years of persistence establishes a permanent cure.

Conditional downstream possibilities include treating hair graying or increasing pigmentation for photoprotection, because these applications may share aspects of melanocyte and stem-cell biology. These are extensions of the concept, not demonstrated consequences in the supplied evidence. Hair pigmentation, epidermal pigmentation and protection against ultraviolet injury would each require separate demonstrations; success in selected vitiligo lesions would not establish those benefits.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central scientific challenge is to establish a functionally renewable melanocyte precursor population where the follicular reservoir has been lost, and support its production of differentiated melanocytes. Restoring visible pigment or detecting cells with precursor-associated markers would not by itself establish that a replacement, self-renewing niche exists. Existing transplantation can supply melanocytes and melanocyte stem cells, so the defining target is regeneration without donor tissue grafting and with demonstrated continuing renewal.

A second barrier is immune survival. The disease environment can deplete epidermal melanocytes and impair melanocyte stem-cell regeneration. An effective regenerative approach must therefore establish cells that persist after temporary immune treatment ends, whether through a separately achieved immune-control capability or another demonstrated means of maintaining local immune homeostasis.

Engineering synthesis: a convincing approach must resolve the origin of the regenerated cells, provide a local environment that supports both precursor maintenance and differentiation, and distribute functional melanocytes sufficiently to restore useful pigmentation. It must also distinguish rebuilding a renewable population from briefly expanding residual cells. These are proposed requirements derived from the target capability; the supplied evidence does not identify a proven implementation or settle which cellular route would work best.

current_state.text: The supplied review identifies the Vitiligo primer by Seneschal and colleagues in Nature Reviews Disease Primers, published on 4 December 2025. Its accessible abstract describes epidermal melanocyte depletion, impaired melanocyte stem-cell regeneration and a central role for tissue-resident memory T cells. Access to the main article was limited to a subscription preview, so these conclusions are attributed to the abstract rather than a full-text assessment. A separately retained complete supplement lists emerging therapies, mechanisms and trial stages; it does not demonstrate or exclude human niche reconstitution.

The review published on 4 January 2024 in Frontiers in Immunology reports that white hair follicles have a lower proportion of intact melanocyte reservoirs than black hair follicles, helping explain difficult repigmentation in leukotrichia. It also describes insufficient local reservoirs as a contributor to refractory disease. However, it reports melanocyte-capable dermal stem cells in hairless vitiligo lesions. That underlying study was not independently supplied or inspected in the evidence review. This distinction prevents treating hairlessness, white hairs or long disease duration as proof of complete precursor depletion.

The 2020 Chinese Medical Journal review by Lei and Hearing describes ultraviolet-associated repigmentation through available follicular, marginal and residual lesional cells. Complete repigmentation can take months or years and may remain unattainable, particularly in glabrous acral skin. These observations establish a dated limitation of treatment responses and their dependence on available cellular sources; they do not establish that every such lesion lacks precursors or that regeneration is presently impossible.

The January 2024 review describes JAK inhibitor efficacy and better facial responses. It also discusses effects beyond recruitment alone: inhibition of inflammatory IFN-γ signaling and enhancement of pigmentation-related Hedgehog and Wnt signaling. These descriptions do not demonstrate creation of a replacement self-renewing niche. The supplied evidence does not establish a ruxolitinib-specific frequency of relapse after withdrawal, so the earlier assertion that withdrawal relapse is common cannot be retained as an established finding here.

Transplantation already replenishes melanocytes and, with some methods, melanocyte stem cells or follicular reservoirs in selected stable vitiligo. The 2024 review describes procedure-dependent limitations, but these do not establish that surgery is categorically scarce or incapable of scaling. Existing graft-based restoration is relevant progress toward cellular replacement; it does not establish the proposed donor-graft-free regeneration capability.

Evidence boundary: none of the supplied reviewed material demonstrates donor-graft-free restoration of a lost, self-renewing melanocyte niche in humans. The packet also contains no bounded freshness search establishing whether that capability remained undemonstrated across human research as of 1 November 2026. Source retrieval dates do not resolve that question. The record therefore supports the biological rationale and the distinctions above, while leaving the current worldwide achievement status open.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical demonstration: achieve clinically meaningful repigmentation without donor tissue grafting in human lesions with documented loss of the follicular melanocyte reservoir, and maintain it for at least two years after all pigmentation-directed and immune-suppressing treatment stops. Temporary immune suppression during establishment could be allowed. Two years is a proposed durability threshold, not an established standard or proof of permanence.
completion_criteria.label: Graft-free repigmentation lasts at least two years after treatment cessation

completion_criteria.text: Proposed biological demonstration: baseline and follow-up tissue assessments should establish the initial reservoir deficit, newly established differentiated melanocytes and a precursor population. Functional evidence should show that the precursor population continues to generate melanocytes over time, beyond marker expression alone. The study should explain how it distinguishes restoration of a renewable population from recruitment or transient expansion of residual cells, including possible dermal precursors.
completion_criteria.label: Restored precursors sustain melanocyte generation beyond transient residual-cell expansion

completion_criteria.text: Proposed selection and comparison requirements: leukotrichia and glabrous vitiligo are useful settings for testing the capability, but neither qualifies automatically as reservoir-depleted. Facial repigmentation where pigmented follicles remain would not establish the target. Comparisons should separate the contributions of regeneration, residual-cell recruitment and immune treatment, and report the extent and persistence of repigmentation by anatomical site.
completion_criteria.label: Comparisons distinguish regeneration from residual-cell recruitment and immune treatment

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: reproduce the result in independent patients and, ideally, independent centers, while reporting treatment burden, adverse effects, recurrence and the evidence for continuing renewal. Define which lesion types and anatomical sites were successfully treated and where results failed or remain unknown. Finite demonstrations would establish that breadth of capability, without proving universal efficacy across vitiligo or indefinite durability.
completion_criteria.label: Independent patients reproduce restoration, with renewal and practical limits reported

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: DER-03, Antigen-selective erasure of pathogenic cutaneous immune memory, is the closest complement. It targets the immune process that could destroy regenerated pigment cells, while DER-08 targets rebuilding the renewable pigment-cell population. Neither capability substitutes for the other in lesions affected by both problems. No DER-03 evidence was supplied, so its achievement status cannot be inferred here.

Roster-based synthesis: DER-01, Clinical restoration of a complete human skin organ, has a broader tissue-restoration goal that could include pigmentation among multiple skin functions. DER-08 isolates the melanocyte lineage and its renewable reservoir. DER-02, One-time genomic cure of severe monogenic skin disease through the epidermal stem-cell compartment, shares an interest in durable stem-cell function but targets correction of inherited disease rather than restoration of a lost melanocyte population.

Roster-based synthesis: DER-04, Programmable passage of macromolecules and gene editors across intact stratum corneum, could provide an enabling delivery route if a future DER-08 approach requires molecular instructions in skin. Delivery alone would not establish precursor renewal or immune survival. DER-05, Epidermal DNA repair sufficient to prevent ultraviolet-driven skin cancer, concerns genomic protection; any photoprotection from restored pigmentation would be a separate outcome and would not establish DNA repair or cancer prevention.

Roster-based synthesis: DER-06, Therapeutic reset of the mutant epidermal field, concerns changing a pathological epidermal cell population, whereas DER-08 seeks to rebuild a pigment-cell population and its renewal capacity. DER-07, A skin-origin intervention that prevents atopic dermatitis and the atopic march, shares a skin–immune interface but addresses prevention of a different disease trajectory. Neither endpoint follows from successful vitiligo repigmentation.

Roster-based synthesis: DER-09, Durable regenerative closure of diabetic foot ulcers after ischemia and pressure are treated, and DER-10, In situ reversal of established keloids and pathological cutaneous scars, share the requirement for durable tissue change rather than a temporary visible response. Their targets remain distinct: wound closure and restoration of pathological scar tissue, respectively, versus melanocyte renewal and pigmentation. Successful DER-08 treatment would not by itself demonstrate either capability.

unresolved_issues: Whether donor-graft-free restoration of a lost, self-renewing melanocyte niche has been demonstrated in humans as of 1 November 2026 remains unresolved because no bounded freshness search was supplied.

The best method for establishing follicular reservoir loss and distinguishing newly established renewal from activation of surviving dermal or other precursors is not specified by the supplied evidence.
The underlying study reporting melanocyte-capable dermal stem cells in hairless lesions was not independently supplied or inspected in the review.
The cellular route and niche-supporting mechanism that could deliver this capability remain unspecified.
Ruxolitinib-specific withdrawal-relapse frequency and the evidence supporting DER-03 cannot be assessed from this packet.

The duration needed to establish clinically sufficient durability, the breadth of responsive anatomical sites and the eventual treatment burden remain open; two years is a proposed demonstration threshold.
Hair-graying treatment, enhanced photoprotection and prevention of ultraviolet-related disease require separate evidence.

brief.title: Lasting skin color after pigment cell reserves are lost
possible: People with vitiligo, a condition that causes skin to lose color, could regain lasting color where hair follicles, the structures that grow hairs, have lost their pigment cell reserves. Treatment would work without grafts of donor tissue.

The skin would regain melanocytes, the cells that make pigment, alongside immature cells that continually produce replacements. Color would persist after any temporary treatment to suppress immune attack ends.
why: For people with too few usable pigment cells, calming inflammation or stimulating surviving cells cannot reliably restore color. Rebuilding a renewable supply would extend treatment beyond reliance on surviving local cells and donor grafts.

sources.showed: Their review describes how immune attack depletes pigment cells and impairs regeneration of their replacements.
sources.quote: This cascade ultimately leads to the depletion of epidermal melanocytes and impairs melanocyte stem cell regeneration.
sources.cited_for: Lasting restoration requires replacement cells that can survive the disease's immune environment.
sources.not_established: The review does not demonstrate rebuilding a lost, renewable pigment cell supply without donor grafts.

sources.who: Xinju Wang, Wei Wu, Jianru Chen, Chunying Li and Shuli Li
sources.showed: Their review reports fewer intact pigment cell reserves in white hair follicles and describes grafting approaches that replenish pigment cells.
sources.quote: Moreover, lesions with white hair are more difficult to get re-pigmentation, since white hair follicles have a lower percentage of intact melanocyte reservoirs than black hair follicles
sources.cited_for: Limited cell reserves help explain why some patches resist treatment, while grafts provide an existing route to cell replacement.
sources.not_established: White hairs do not prove complete reserve loss, and grafting does not establish restoration without donor tissue.

sources.who: Tie-Chi Lei and Vincent J. Hearing
sources.showed: Their review describes how ultraviolet light treatment restores color through available cells in hair follicles and surrounding skin.
sources.cited_for: Responses to light treatment depend on available pigment cell sources.
sources.not_established: Restoring color from surviving cells does not demonstrate rebuilding a lost, self-renewing supply.

shown: Existing treatments can restore color using surviving cells. Grafts can also replenish pigment cells in selected stable cases, as Wang and colleagues describe. These results do not establish lasting renewal without grafts where hair-follicle reserves have been lost.
missing: A treatment would need to rebuild a renewable pigment cell supply without donor grafts where hair-follicle reserves are demonstrably lost.
The replacement supply would need to keep producing working pigment cells, beyond briefly multiplying surviving cells.
Restored cells and useful skin color would need to survive after temporary immune treatment ends.

milestones.label: Restored color lasts after all treatment stops
milestones.explanation: Meaningful color would have to persist for at least two years without donor grafts after all pigment-directed and immune-suppressing treatment ends, in skin with proven reserve loss. This would establish sustained benefit.

milestones.label: Replacement cells keep producing pigment cells
milestones.explanation: Tissue studies would have to establish initial reserve loss and a restored immature cell supply that keeps making pigment cells. This would distinguish renewal from briefly expanding survivors.

milestones.label: Comparisons separate rebuilding from surviving cells and immune treatment
milestones.explanation: Comparisons would have to confirm reserve loss, separate cell rebuilding from surviving-cell recruitment and immune treatment, and report lasting color by body site. This would establish what caused restoration and where it works.

milestones.label: Other patients reproduce restoration and reveal practical limits
milestones.explanation: Results would have to recur in independent patients, ideally across centers, with continuing renewal, burden, harms, recurrence and successful or failed sites reported. This would establish reproducibility and practical reach.

uncertain: The best way to prove reserve loss and distinguish rebuilding from activation of surviving cells remains unsettled.
The cellular route and local conditions needed to sustain a replacement supply remain unknown.
Two years is a proposed durability threshold; the necessary duration and range of responsive body sites remain open.

page.title: Melanocyte stem-cell reconstitution in reservoir-depleted skin
page.definition: Human vitiligo lesions with documented loss of follicular melanocyte reserves regain self-renewing precursors that supply melanocytes, the pigment-producing cells. The restored population and skin colour persist after temporary treatment ends, without donor tissue grafting.

goal.need: A 2017 meta-analysis of 35 studies and 1,428 patients quantified responses to ultraviolet phototherapy; the table gives its narrow-band ultraviolet B results. Insufficient local melanocyte reservoirs are a reported obstacle to repigmentation. Existing surgery supplies melanocytes or their precursors by transplantation; rebuilding the reserve without donor grafts would address the cell-supply problem.

figures.caption: Rates of at least 75% repigmentation with narrow-band ultraviolet B phototherapy.
figures.note: The time points pool different sets of studies and do not measure within-patient change. Searches ended on 26 January 2016. Participants were studied for generalized vitiligo, without a requirement for documented follicular reservoir loss.

statements.quote: Stable vitiligo needs treatment to regenerate epidermal melanocytes from the hair follicle or interfollicular precursors
statements.context: The recommendation concerns epidermal regeneration from precursors; it does not define reconstruction of a depleted follicular reservoir.

statements.quote: Treatment is defined as successful if repigmentation exceeds 80% and at least 80% of the gained repigmentation is maintained for over 6 months.
statements.context: This defines clinical repigmentation success, without establishing stem-cell renewal or requiring treatment withdrawal.

completion.title: A reconstituted human melanocyte reservoir sustains repigmentation for over six months off treatment.
completion.criterion: In human vitiligo lesions with documented follicular reservoir loss, an intervention without donor tissue grafting establishes self-renewing precursors that continue to generate functional melanocytes. Cellular-origin and functional evidence must establish a rebuilt precursor compartment, beyond pigment production by surviving reservoirs alone. Repigmentation exceeds 80% of the treated lesion, and at least 80% of that gain remains for over six months after pigmentation-directed treatment and temporary immune treatment stop. Renewal remains demonstrable during that interval. White hairs or hairlessness alone do not document reservoir loss.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas synthesis; no outside body was found defining this combined biological and clinical test. VGICC supplies the repigmentation percentages and observation duration, but not the reservoir-reconstruction or treatment-withdrawal requirements.
completion.basis: Searches of VGICC criteria, International Vitiligo Task Force recommendations, ISSCR standards, FDA-related sources, ClinicalTrials.gov and primary niche studies found no combined test for verified reservoir loss, graft-free reconstitution, renewal and persistence off treatment. This Atlas test uses the functional stem-cell definition and VGICC's clinical success thresholds. Applying those thresholds specifically after treatment withdrawal is an Atlas condition; six months does not establish permanence.

milestones.title: Melanocyte precursors self-renew and generate pigment-producing descendants in laboratory assays.
milestones.criterion: Precursors maintain an undifferentiated population while producing functional melanocytes. The functional test is self-renewal plus lineage differentiation, without an established numerical duration cutoff. Kumar et al. reported self-renewal and melanocyte differentiation in cultured dermal cells from glabrous vitiligo lesions in 2016; the accessible abstract gives no donor count. This identifies a possible residual source, rather than demonstrating reconstruction of a depleted follicular niche.
milestones.set_by: Functional stem-cell definition used by Nishimura et al. in Nature (2002), and applied to human lesional dermal precursors by Kumar et al. (2016). ISSCR supplies general functional-validation criteria for stem-cell models.
milestones.threshold_quote: capacity to self-renew and generate differentiated progeny

milestones.title: Melanocyte-lineage cells repopulate vacant mouse follicular niches and function there as stem cells.
milestones.criterion: Melanocyte-lineage cells colonize vacant mouse follicular niches, maintain undifferentiated precursors and regenerate pigment-producing progeny on subsequent hair growth. Nishimura et al. reported this in K14-SLF;Dct-lacZ mice on 25 April 2002; animal numbers for this experiment were not stated.
milestones.set_by: Functional niche-repopulation assay used by Nishimura et al., Nature (2002). This experimental test was published for mouse hair follicles; it is not a human clinical threshold.
milestones.threshold_quote: retain sufficient self-renewing capability to function as stem cells after repopulation into vacant niches.

milestones.title: Graft-free treatment rebuilds a renewing reservoir and repigments over 80% of a human vitiligo lesion.
milestones.criterion: A human vitiligo lesion with tissue evidence of follicular reservoir loss acquires a self-renewing precursor population and functional melanocytes without donor tissue grafting. Cellular-origin and functional evidence establish a rebuilt precursor compartment, beyond pigment production by surviving reservoirs alone. More than 80% of the treated lesion repigments. VGICC supplies the percentage threshold; the reservoir-loss and renewal conditions are Atlas-defined. This is the human result before the off-treatment observation period. No qualifying human demonstration was found.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas synthesis; no published first-in-human criterion combining verified reservoir depletion, graft-free reconstitution and functional renewal was found. The repigmentation percentage comes from VGICC's general treatment-success definition.

not_found: No outside-body completion test or clinical milestone sequence specifically for graft-free reconstruction of a depleted human follicular melanocyte reservoir was found.
No validated criterion establishing complete follicular reservoir loss throughout a human lesion was found.
No human demonstration combining verified reservoir loss, graft-free functional renewal and persistence after treatment withdrawal was found.
Donor numbers were absent from the accessible abstract of Kumar et al.; mouse numbers were not stated for the niche-repopulation experiment in the accessible Nishimura et al. text.
The ClinicalTrials.gov search page could not be opened, although a transplantation-study protocol was accessible.
The 2025 Nature Reviews Disease Primers publisher page redirected to an inaccessible authentication page.
The 2020 Chinese Medical Journal publisher page returned a payment error; its PMC page was accessible.

results.finding: Neonatal foreskin dermal cells from 3 cell lines self-renewed and generated pigmented melanocytes; 3 of 960 single cells reformed spheres.
results.detail: The cells were multipotent dermal precursors from foreskin, not vitiligo lesions. Pigmentation was demonstrated in a 3D skin reconstruct.
results.quote: These dermal stem cells, grown as three-dimensional spheres, displayed a capacity for self-renewal and expressed NGFRp75, nestin and OCT4, but not melanocyte markers. In addition, cells derived from single-cell clones were able to differentiate into multiple lineages including melanocytes.

results.finding: Dct-lacZ transgenic mice (n not stated) showed self-maintenance and progeny regeneration at early anagen; no numerical duration cutoff.
results.detail: Mouse study; animal numbers not stated. Shows melanocyte-lineage stem-cell self-maintenance and progeny regeneration in hair follicles, but not human vitiligo reservoir reconstitution.
results.quote: It is only the population in this region that fulfils the criteria for stem cells, being immature, slow cycling, self-maintaining and fully competent in regenerating progeny on activation at early anagen (the growing phase of hair follicles).

results.finding: K14-SLF;Dct-lacZ mice (n not stated) showed repopulation of vacant niches and stem-cell function; no numerical threshold.
results.detail: Mouse study; animal numbers not stated. Shows melanocyte-lineage progeny migrate from the niche, repopulate vacant niches, and function as stem cells, satisfying the mouse niche criterion.
results.quote: Induction of the re-pigmentation process in K14-steel factor transgenic mice demonstrates that a portion of amplifying stem-cell progeny can migrate out from the niche and retain sufficient self-renewing capability to function as stem cells after repopulation into vacant niches.

results.finding: Sorted CD34- vs CD34+ McSCs (n not stated): 25% pigmented CD34- cells at day 7 vs 5% CD34+ in melanocyte differentiation medium; self-renewal not shown.
results.detail: In vitro pigmented differentiation is reported, but the text does not demonstrate serial self-renewal or sustained undifferentiated precursor maintenance; CD34- cells were more melanogenic.
results.quote: The percentage of pigmented cells from CD34+ cells increased from 0 to 5% from day 4 to day 7, while this percentage increased from 2% to 25% for CD34- cells introduced into the culture environment.

results.finding: CD34- McSCs repigmented 4/4 amelanocytic Mitf Mi-wh/Mi-wh mouse skin grafts, with durable pigmentation over 6 months (CD34+ 3/4).
results.detail: Mouse amelanocytic skin-graft model; both CD34+ and CD34- cells populated bulge/SHG niches after reconstitution.
results.quote: 3/4 grafts of CD34+ cells and 4/4 grafts of CD34- cells demonstrated pigmentation at two months following graft placement. Pigmentation within the grafts was sustained, with durable pigmentation observed over 6 months.
